_note: City pulse: short, anonymised takes on what Bengalureans argue about, by topic. These sample lines are team-written placeholders. scripts/build_voice.py builds pulse.json from the team's field notes: what we learned reading Reddit, Instagram and real conversations, in our own words, with no usernames and nothing copied.

rent: Landlords asking 10 months deposit is normal here and nobody questions it.
Rents near tech parks jump every time a new company announces a campus.
Brokers charge a month's rent just to show a flat with a leaking bathroom.
People move further out to save rent and then lose two hours a day in traffic.
Bachelors get rejected by landlords for no reason other than being bachelors.
jobs: New campuses bring jobs, but the roads and water supply never keep up.
Hiring news is great until you see the traffic on the road to the new office.
Every new tech park means the nearby darshinis and PGs raise prices.
Freshers are hopeful again whenever big companies announce hiring.
layoffs: Layoff season makes everyone check their savings and their notice period.
When tech jobs go, the auto drivers, PG owners and restaurants feel it next.
People are tired of companies calling layoffs 'restructuring'.
cost: Metro fare hikes push people back to bikes and cabs, and traffic gets worse.
Every fare or fuel hike hits daily-wage workers and students the hardest.
People say Bengaluru has become as expensive as Mumbai without the transport.
Taxes on companies always end up being paid by ordinary people somehow.
traffic: Silk Board is a rite of passage for anyone who has lived here a year.
An 8 km commute taking over an hour is considered a good day on ORR.
Metro expansion is the only thing people are genuinely hopeful about.
flood: One heavy rain and the same underpasses flood every single year.
People in low-lying areas move their bikes to higher ground when it rains.
